capabilities.name: App Interface & Reporting
capabilities.notes: Provides native mobile UI for map visualization and navigation. However, it lacks the specific 'Team Leader' reporting features (diary submission, alert acknowledgement) required by the component. It is a consumer-grade mapping app, not a tactical team coordination tool.

capabilities.name: Offline Map Support
capabilities.notes: Core feature of the application. Explicitly designed for offline use with OpenStreetMap data.

capabilities.name: Push Notifications
capabilities.notes: The README explicitly states 'No push notifications' as a privacy feature. The app is designed to be offline-first and does not include FCM/APNS integration for incoming alerts.

capabilities.name: Turn-by-Turn Navigation
capabilities.notes: Supports walking, cycling, and car navigation with voice guidance.

capabilities.name: Map Search & Routing
capabilities.notes: Fast offline search and routing capabilities are core features.

capabilities.name: Track Management
capabilities.notes: Supports import/export of KML, KMZ, GPX, GeoJSON formats.

constraints: Requires significant storage for map tiles
No internet connection required for core functionality

assumptions: Assumes ability to fork the C++ core and rewrite Android/iOS UI layers completely.
Assumes 'No push notifications' constraint can be overridden by integrating FCM/APNS, which contradicts the project's privacy philosophy.
Assumes custom backend integration for diary/alert submission is built externally as this app has no networking stack for user data.

evidence.claim: Organic Maps is an offline maps app with no push notifications or tracking.
Project uses C++ and supports Android/iOS platforms.
Build system is CMake with Android Gradle integration.

description: Organic Maps is a privacy-focused, offline-capable mobile mapping application for Android and iOS. It provides detailed map visualization, turn-by-turn navigation, search, and track management using OpenStreetMap data. It explicitly excludes cloud connectivity features such as push notifications, user accounts, or telemetry.
deployment_constraints: Requires significant storage for map tiles
No internet connection required for core functionality
known_gaps: No Push Notification support (FCM/APNS) - explicitly excluded by design.
No WebSocket support for real-time alert relay.
No HTTPS POST API for diary entry or position report submission.
No 'Team Leader' specific UI or workflow.
No user authentication or account management.
risks: License: Apache 2.0 is permissive, but the app's privacy-first design may conflict with defense requirements for data reporting.
Maintenance: Forking a consumer app to add enterprise features may lead to divergence and high maintenance costs.
Security: The app explicitly avoids network connectivity; adding it introduces attack surface not originally designed for.

adaptation_assumptions: Assumes ability to fork the C++ core and rewrite Android/iOS UI layers completely.
Assumes 'No push notifications' constraint can be overridden by integrating FCM/APNS, which contradicts the project's privacy philosophy.
Assumes custom backend integration for diary/alert submission is built externally as this app has no networking stack for user data.
